rounds.text: Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 17.3x [E1], which sits slightly below its sector benchmark of 18.49x [E6], offering investors a compelling entry point relative to its growth trajectory. The business demonstrates exceptional operational efficiency, boasting an ROA of 7.64% [E8], an ROE of 15.96% [E9], and a robust ROCE of 17.31% [E10] that drastically outperform broader sector benchmarks of 1.93%, 5.15%, and 5.62% respectively. This strong profitability is underpinned by impressive compounding, evidenced by a 3-year profit growth rate of 117% [E18], trailing twelve-month profit growth of 75% [E19], and an expanding operating margin that reached 30% [E23]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is clearly surging, demonstrated by positive money flows and a substantial 9.34 percentage point increase in combined foreign and domestic institutional holdings over a single quarter [E35, E36, E37]. Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -461 Cr, resulting in a weak cash conversion of -1.64x [E27, E28]. Management nevertheless maintains strong operational momentum, guiding for over 40% AUM growth [E85] and a 100 basis point reduction in borrowing costs for the second half of the fiscal year [E86].

The most glaring vulnerability in Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd is the profound disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, highlighted by an alarming cash conversion ratio of -1.64x and negative operating cash flow of Rs -461 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -471 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28, E29]. Compounding these liquidity pressures, promoters have trimmed their stake to 20.42% in October 2026 from 24.80% in June 2026 [E34], while the stock price languishes below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43] amid high annualized volatility of 54.4% [E46]. Furthermore, management's own admissions reveal acute underlying stress in the credit ecosystem, including softening quality among new customers [E70], rising distress in small-ticket loans [E69], and precautionary lending halts across roughly 450 pin codes [E83], while the company refuses to reward shareholders with any dividend yield [E4]. Conceded: the company boasts a robust 5-year compounded sales growth of 66% [E14], high institutional inflows of 9.34 percentage points [E37], and a significant reduction in borrowings to Rs 1,643 Cr by September 2026 [E32].

Conceded: cash conversion is negative at -1.64x with operating cash flow at Rs -461 Cr and free cash flow at Rs -471 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28, E29]. However, this liquidity picture must be read against borrowings falling sharply to Rs 1,643 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 2,429 Cr a year earlier [E32], alongside a fortified NBFC capital adequacy of 40.2% driven by a successful IPO and fresh equity infusion [E80, E81]. Conceded: promoter holdings declined to 20.42% and the stock trades below its moving averages with 54.4% volatility [E34, E43, E46], but institutional money flow is strongly positive with a holding change of +9.34 percentage points [E37]. Conceded: management highlighted industry stress and preemptively paused lending in 450 pin codes [E69, E70, E83], yet they have already reopened roughly 40% of those pin codes as signals turned positive [E83], while maintaining firm guidance for over 40% AUM growth and a 15% reduction in credit costs [E67, E88]. Finally, the zero dividend yield [E4] simply reflects aggressive capital reinvestment to fund a robust 5-year compounded sales growth of 66% [E14] and operating margin expansion to 30% [E23].

Conceded: borrowings fell to Rs 1,643 Cr [E32] and capital adequacy rose to 40.2% [E80]. However, pointing to a stronger balance sheet does not erase the alarming reality that operating cash flow and free cash flow plunged to catastrophic deficits of Rs -461 Cr and Rs -471 Cr respectively, yielding an abysmal cash conversion of -1.64x [E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: institutional holdings increased [E37], but this influx has failed to prevent promoters from slashing their stake to a low 20.42% while shedding 4.38 percentage points in a single quarter [E34, E54], highlighting insider abandonment while outside capital steps in. Conceded: management reopened 40% of the paused pin codes [E83], but the very fact that early warning systems forced a halt across 450 pin codes underscores acute, underlying vulnerability in their small-ticket portfolio amid industry-wide stress where borrower quality is rapidly softening [E69, E70, E83]. Finally, while the bull defends zero dividends [E4] as reinvestment for growth [E14], this excuse rings hollow against an annualised volatility of 54.4% and a price languishing below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43, E46].

evidence.quote: Now simple mathematics will tell you that if we have already grown 13% in one quarter, you know, we are only going to overachieve that. So the point I was making on guidance is we remain firmly confident of over-delivering on the number that we had given last quarter of 40%.

evidence.fact: Management firmly holds to the guidance of a 15% reduction in credit cost.
evidence.quote: We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost, and we are tracking well on that.

evidence.fact: Management stated they remain firmly on track for the FY27 guidance set out on parameters including AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability.
evidence.quote: On the guidance for future, we remain firmly on track for the FY27 guidance we set out on different parameters, be it AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability including ROE and ROA.

evidence.fact: Management noted that bureau data for the industry reveals a clear divergence beneath a calm surface, with stress building in small-ticket loans and among borrowers carrying debt across multiple lenders.
evidence.quote: The bureau data for the industry now shows a clear divergence beneath a calm surface. Talking about industry, headline asset quality looks benign, yet beneath the surface, stress is building, concentrated in a few places, particularly in the small ticket loans or instances of borrowers carrying debt across several lenders at once, and households taking new lines only to service old ones.

evidence.fact: Management observed that for the industry, the quality of new customers has softened even as headline delinquencies in personal loans improved.
evidence.quote: For the industry, the quality of new customers has softened even as headline delinquencies in personal loans have improved - both are true at once.

evidence.fact: Management remains optimistic about India's long-term structural credit opportunity while remaining realistic about near-term conditions.
evidence.quote: As we look ahead to FY27, we remain optimistic about India's long-term structural credit opportunity. Many reasons for that, not only economic growth that the country will see, but also the huge degree of credit under penetration which exists, while at the same time being realistic and cautious about near-term conditions.

evidence.fact: The Loan Against Property (LAP) AUM stands at INR 617 crores across 101 branches in eight states.
evidence.quote: LAP business which we started two years back, the AUM stands at INR 617 crores across 101 branches in eight states, about 7.7% of the total AUM.

evidence.fact: The company has begun building capabilities in mutual fund distribution and its subsidiary has secured an AMFI registration.
evidence.quote: Separately, we have begun to build capabilities in mutual fund distribution. The rationale for this, is a large proportion of our customers have invested in SIPs and mutual funds over time. An offering like this will help serve them well and enhance our fee income. Our subsidiary has secured an AMFI registration already.

evidence.fact: The company plans to add at least 80 more branches for the LAP business by the end of the financial year.
evidence.quote: We plan to have at least 80 more branches by end of this financial year.

evidence.fact: Pre-provisioning operating profit was INR 256 crores, up 42% year-on-year.
evidence.quote: Pre-provisioning operating profit was INR 256 crores, which is up 42% year-on-year.

evidence.fact: Opex as a proportion of AUM came down from 19.9% to 18.0%.
evidence.quote: You must have seen the operating leverage some evidence of that, 19.9% cost which was opex as a proportion of AUM has already come down to 18.0% percent.

evidence.fact: Registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million, and customer count reached 12.25 million, up 26% year-on-year.
evidence.quote: The registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million. We have now served 12.25 million customers, an increase of 26% year-on-year.

evidence.fact: Loan Against Property AUM stands at nearly ₹ 518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states.
evidence.quote: LAP AUM stands at nearly ₹ 518 crore, across 98 branches in 8 states, contributing 7.3% of total AUM.

evidence.fact: On-book AUM stands at ₹ 3,556 crore supported by more than 45 lending partners.
evidence.quote: On-book AUM stands at ₹ 3,556 crore, supported by 45+ lending partners, where cost of borrowing has been between 11.5% and 14.25%.

evidence.fact: Capital adequacy in the NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter following the IPO.
evidence.quote: Capital adequacy in our NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter. Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crores, nearly four times its level in March 2023, built on retained earnings, organic profitability, and the IPO completed in May 2026.

evidence.fact: Approximately ₹ 630 crore of the primary issue has already been infused as fresh equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital.
evidence.quote: 75% of the primary issue, approximately ₹ 630 crore have been already infused as fresh equity into our NBFC subsidiary, which is Si Creva Capital.

evidence.fact: Management noted that West Asia poses a potential risk through higher oil prices, shipping costs, and customer confidence transmission.
evidence.quote: The first is West Asia, where the risk is not geography but transmission through higher oil prices, the cost of shipping, and, over time, the confidence of the customer.

evidence.fact: Based on early warning systems, the company paused lending across approximately 450 pin codes last quarter, and has since reopened about 40% of them.
evidence.quote: Just to give you an instance, last quarter, out of caution, we paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes based on what our early warning system had flagged. We have re-examined those pin codes since. The signals have turned modestly positive, and we have reopened approximately 40% of these pin codes already.

evidence.fact: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.
evidence.quote: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 12 months): Management stated they remain confident of over-delivering on the full-year AUM growth guidance of upwards of 40%.
evidence.quote: So the point I was making on guidance is we remain firmly confident of over-delivering on the number that we had given last quarter of 40%.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (H2 FY27): Management anticipates the cost of borrowing to drop by a minimum of 100 basis points in the second half of the fiscal year.
evidence.quote: So our guidance for FY, particularly H2 of FY27, that you will see the cost of borrowing dropping by 100 basis points and it will only increase as we, as the old debt basically runs off the book, right?

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): Management expects the Loan Against Property business to achieve breakeven around the third quarter of the year.
evidence.quote: Somewhere around Q3 of this year, it will only be delivering the desired ROE for which we started the business.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): Management targets AUM growth of over 40% for FY27.
evidence.quote: We expect to grow at north of 40% in AUM, with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection, while secured business scale-up is also expected to be strong.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Management targets gross NPA below 2.25% and impairment cost reduction of 10%-15%.
evidence.quote: On asset quality, we are targeting gross NPA below 2.25%, year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%, and continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.
